Q1: Perfluoro-2,3-dimethylbutane exhibits several potential hazards that require an expanded perspective beyond formal GHS classifications, including acute and chronic environmental, inhalation, oral, and dermal/eye hazards (Tier 2). However, its carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive hazards (CMR), endocrine disruption, and organ/systemic hazards are currently categorized as data deficient (Tier 4), indicating a lack of sufficient information for a confident assessment.
Q2: Perfluoro-2,3-dimethylbutane is identified on the EPA PFAS 2024 list, indicating its classification as a Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substance. This inclusion highlights regulatory attention regarding its presence and potential impacts within this significant class of chemicals.
Q3: While Perfluoro-2,3-dimethylbutane has a well-defined molecular formula (C6F14) and substance class, its overall characterization is limited, with only 52 literature references, which is considerably below the median for studied chemicals. Furthermore, three of its seven hazard categories are classified as data deficient (Tier 4), suggesting significant gaps in the comprehensive understanding of its hazard profile.
